original_question: If f is a polynomial automorphism of C^d with λ(f) = 1 and the degree sequence deg(f^n) is unbounded, does there exist a constant C > 0 such that deg(f^n) ≥ C n?
target_in_paper: Section 10.1, Question 40. The paper asks: suppose λ(f)=1 and deg(f^n) is unbounded for a polynomial automorphism f of ℂ^d; does there exist C>0 such that deg(f^n)≥Cn? It is introduced there as a weaker form of the preceding Question 39. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~buff/Preprints/Henon/Henon.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact target almost verbatim: it has the right ambient space ℂ^d, the correct hypotheses λ(f)=1 and unboundedness of the degree sequence (deg(f^n)), and the exact conclusion asking for a linear lower bound deg(f^n)≥Cn. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~buff/Preprints/Henon/Henon.pdf))
missing_details: Define the dynamical degree explicitly: λ(f):=lim_{n→∞}(deg(f^n))^{1/n}, which is introduced immediately before Questions 38–40. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~buff/Preprints/Henon/Henon.pdf))

State what deg(f) means: for a polynomial automorphism written in coordinates, deg(f) is the maximum total degree of its coordinate polynomials; §10.1 uses this notation after recalling the degree definition from §6.1. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~buff/Preprints/Henon/Henon.pdf))
Make the iteration index explicit, e.g. n≥1 and the degree sequence means (deg(f^n))_{n≥1}. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~buff/Preprints/Henon/Henon.pdf))

If you want the formulation to reflect the paper's local context, note that this is the weaker version of Question 39, which asks whether deg(f^n) has polynomial growth deg(f^n)≍n^k and, when k≥1, whether f preserves a rational fibration. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~buff/Preprints/Henon/Henon.pdf))

No extra assumptions such as tameness, regularity, homogeneity, bounded algebraic degree of f, nilpotency conditions, or preservation of a rational fibration belong to Question 40 itself. The rational-fibration clause appears only in Question 39. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~buff/Preprints/Henon/Henon.pdf))
refined_question: Let f:ℂ^d→ℂ^d be a polynomial automorphism, let deg(f) denote the maximum total degree of its coordinate polynomials, and define its dynamical degree by λ(f):=lim_{n→∞}(deg(f^n))^{1/n}. Assume that λ(f)=1 and that the degree sequence (deg(f^n))_{n≥1} is unbounded. Must there exist a constant C>0 such that deg(f^n)≥Cn for all n≥1?
justification: This is Question 40 in §10.1, not the broader neighboring Question 39. Your draft matches the paper's official formulation almost exactly; the only real gaps are the explicit definition of λ(f), the meaning of deg(f), and the iteration quantifier. The surrounding paragraph is exactly the relevant context: it defines λ(f), notes earlier lower bounds of Urech and Cantat–Xie, and then states Question 40 as the weaker form of Question 39. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~buff/Preprints/Henon/Henon.pdf))
